cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has been kneeling before the altar of the LORD with his hands spread out toward heaven, praying one LONG prayer. Friend, if this prayer were a voicemail, the phone would've cut him off three times. Now he's finally finished, and he gets up.

cards.question: Solomon stands up in front of the whole assembly of Israel. What does he do?

answers.text: He blesses them in a loud voice
He reads them the book of the law
He names his son the next king

cards.text: First thing out of his mouth: "Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised."

cards.question: Solomon says some of the good promises God made through His servant Moses have failed.

cards.text: Not one word failed. NOT ONE. I can't even keep my promise to stop sneaking cookie dough, and God kept EVERY single one.

cards.question: Then Solomon prays, "May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers." What else does he ask?

answers.text: That He never leaves or forsakes them
That He makes them the richest nation
That He wins every battle for them

cards.text: Next, Solomon prays about their insides. He asks the LORD to incline their hearts to Himself, which is smart, because left on its own, my heart inclines straight toward the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to turn their hearts so they will walk in all His ___ and keep His ___.

cards.text: Then Solomon asks that the words of his prayer stay near to the LORD day and night. That way God will uphold the cause of His servant and His people Israel.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to uphold their cause as each ___ requires.
Solomon wants God to uphold Israel's cause so that only Israel will know the LORD is God.

cards.text: All the peoples of the earth, so they'll know the LORD is God, and then Solomon adds, "There is no other!" Exclamation point and everything, friend. That's not a suggestion. That's a mic drop.

cards.question: Solomon ends by telling the people to keep their hearts fully devoted to the LORD, walking in His statutes and keeping His commandments. What does he say about their hearts right now?

answers.text: They are still far from Him

cards.text: Blessing done. Then the king and all Israel with him offer sacrifices before the LORD, and friend, Solomon does NOT do small.

cards.question: Solomon offers 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep as peace offerings to the LORD.

cards.text: A hundred and twenty THOUSAND sheep. I spent years counting dust in the back of a junk drawer, and I never got anywhere near that number.

cards.question: With all these offerings, what do the king and all the Israelites do with the house of the LORD?

cards.text: On that same day, Solomon consecrates the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD. Right there he offers the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the fat of the peace offerings.

cards.question: Solomon uses the courtyard because the bronze altar before the LORD is too ___ to hold all these offerings.

cards.text: Then comes the feast. Solomon and all Israel keep it before the LORD, a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt.

cards.question: The great assembly at Solomon's feast stretches from Lebo-hamath all the way to the Brook of Egypt. What does that tell us about who came?

answers.text: People came from across the land
Mostly visitors from other nations came

cards.question: Solomon and all Israel keep the feast before the LORD for fourteen days in all.

cards.text: On the fifteenth day, Solomon sends the people away. He blessed them at the start, and now they bless the king right back on their way out the door.

cards.question: As the people head home from Solomon's feast, how are they feeling?

answers.text: Sad that the feast is over

cards.question: Why are the people so glad as they go home?

answers.text: For the good the LORD did for David and Israel
For the gifts the king handed out to them
For the rain that finally came on the land

cards.text: The temple's dedicated, the people are home, and everybody's smiling. But hold on to your apron, friend, because this story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: The voicemail joke makes the length of Solomon's prayer (1 Kings 8:22-53, which is Scripture) the punchline. It reads as a dig at a Bible prayer, not as respect for Solomon's human situation.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: "Then Solomon prays" and "What else does he ask?" Verse 55 says Solomon blessed the whole assembly, saying "May the LORD our God be with us..." (8:57). The text calls this a blessing spoken to the people, not a prayer.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: "Solomon prays about their insides. He asks the LORD to incline their hearts" recasts the blessing in 8:58 ("May He incline our hearts to Himself") as a prayer or request to God.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: "Solomon asks God to turn their hearts" recasts the blessing in 8:58 ("May He incline our hearts...") as a request to God.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: The two right answers can swap places and still sound right: "walk in all His commandments and keep His ways." A baker could argue that the swapped order is also correct.
findings.question: On a two-blank fill in the blank, must each right answer fit only its own blank? Should the no-near-matches rule also cover the right answers fitting each other's blanks?

findings.problem: "Solomon asks that..." and "That way God will uphold the cause..." turn the wish "may these words... be near... so that He may uphold" (8:59) into a request and then a certain outcome. The text keeps it as a hoped-for "may."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording "as each day requires" (8:59), with day, year or season as choices. Nothing in the setup lets a baker reason it out. Card 9's "day and night" only hints at the word. This card also uses "Solomon asks God," which recasts the blessing as a request.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer "They are devoted this day" carries the Bible-sounding phrase "this day." The wrong answers ("They have already wandered", "They are still far from Him") don't sound like that, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer "Joyful and glad in heart" is the Bible's own wording (8:66). The wrong answers ("Sad that the feast is over", "Worried about the long trip") are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The first sentence ("The temple's dedicated, the people are home, and everybody's smiling.") recaps what was already told and adds nothing from 8:66. Verse 66 was already asked on choice cards 11 and 12, so this card should be only the story-isn't-over line.

rule.text: No recap cards. ... When the passage's last verse is asked on a choice card, the last story card can be just this line.
